faces.f: Once you have ascended to the highest temple of Orazca, the power of the Immortal Sun is yours to wield forever.

"The soldier's path is worn smooth by the tread of many feet—all in one direction, none returning."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"My family sheltered in her light, the dark was content to wait."
—Crovax

Hanna: "We must learn how they protect each other."
Mirri: "After they're done trying to kill us, all right?"

"I always charge a little extra to take on a pegasus. They fly like eagles, kick like mules, and hide like hermits."
—Tahli *en*-Dal, bounty hunter
The auratog enjoys eating its wards.

"Faith's shield is hammered out by the blows of unbelievers."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

When the eagle catches a cloud, it tears it into strips that fall to earth.
—Vec myth of the rains
The swarm seemed unmoved by the artificial slivers' destruction. "They clearly were not the leaders," Hanna cursed. "I guess we'll have to do this the hard way."

"Precision is frequently more valuable than force."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
"Forgive me," Mirri whispered. "I thought you a burden, and you saved my life." Hanna quietly accepted the apology.
Gerrard grinned and drew his sword. "This won't be a fair fight," he called to his crew. "They should have brought a second ship!"

"I protect the Legacy with my life if necessary, for its purpose is far more important than my own."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator

"Destiny, chance, fate, fortune—they're all just ways of claiming your successes without claiming your failures."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

"One cannot cleanse the wounds of failure."
—Karn, silver golem

Flash like daybreak to the fray.
—Motto of the Knights of Dawn

"I do not miss sunlight. The very memory of it burns my eyes."
—Volrath

"Strapping on nine hundred pounds of armor every morning would make any warrior cross."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

"A skilled decoy can throw your enemies off your trail. A master decoy can survive to do it again."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

"As usual, there will be time for prayer only *after* the worst happens."
—Orim, Samite healer

"The silkworm spins itself a new existence. So the healer weaves the threads of life."
—Orim, Samite healer
Frozen by conscience, Karn did not resist as the moggs carried him to the *Predator*.

The first Rath-born pegasus was so offended by the sky that it hid its eyes in the earth.
—Vec lore
"The cannon wasn't aimed at you!" pleaded Vhati. "I'm not sure which is more pathetic," replied Greven, "your judgment or your aim."

"I'm amused by wasted effort when it's not my own."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator

"A sacrifice made in peace is worth a dozen made in panic."
—Orim, Samite healer

"Carry war to the Dauthi, no matter the way, no matter the world."
—Soltari battle chant
Alone at the portal, Ertai began his meditation. He realized immediately that he was not alone.

"Children of the Ruins, raised to be warriors, know that life begins when another speaks their names."
—Soltari *Tales of Life*

"In times of war the victors rarely save their best for last."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

"Prayer rarely explains."
—Orim, Samite healer
"In Rath," the priest said, "there is even greater need for prayer."

"Dauthi blood is Soltari wine."
—Soltari *Tales of Life*

"Hold your position! Leave doubt for the dying!"
—Tahngarth of the *Weatherlight*
"Keep them at sword's length!" Gerrard's order fell flat as each sliver's talon suddenly grew longer. "Hold on—break out the polearms!"

"Flame grows gentle with but a little distance."
—Orim, Samite healer

"There shall be a vast shout and then a vaster silence."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"Deep devourer concealed in darkhome
Shrouded it seeks all becomes fodder
Once we swam alone and asea
But no more."
—*Rootwater Saga*

"Temper, temper."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"It was probably a lousy spell in the first place."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"There is nothing you can do that I cannot simply deny."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"The sanctity of poverty is an invention of the rich."
—Starke
Two things are needed to survive the harsh skies of Rath: a thick hide and a thicker skull.

"It's hard to hurt anyone when you're as transparent as your motives."
—Ertai, wizard adept
During the giant crabs' mating season, Skyshroud nights are filled with the clatter of their skirmishes.

"So like men are they: a hardened shell with fragile flesh beneath."
—Selenia, dark angel

"We can fight with you or against you. After my day, I'd prefer the former."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
Squee tucked the warm ball in his pocket and slipped a pebble in its place. 'Glok,' he mumbled, and hid.

"And when this land is wasted, where will we go?"
—Thalakos lament

"Water is firmament to the finned."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
From its maw comes neither word nor whisper—only wind.

"Part of me believes that Barrin taught me meditation simply to shut me up."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"A jigsaw puzzle that lives, breeds, and thinks."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator
A gleam like struggling sunlight penetrated Selenia's dark thoughts.

"You've failed Gerrard. You've failed the Legacy. You've failed yourself. I can do no more."
—Volrath, to Karn

"Drop a dagger into the murky deep and the merfolk will cut your throat with it."
—Skyshroud saying

"Bitter water vicious wave
Shadow-cold shallows root-made maze
Home's angry embrace."
—*Rootwater Saga*

"Ugh! When did orcs and fish start having kids?"
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
Water is life. Or perhaps it is just something to wash it down with.
The brighter the wings, the deeper the impact crater.

Condor's flight augurs sleepless night.
—Skyshroud proverb
Call it the thinking mage's version of brute force.

"Why should I flatter another with imitation when I can satisfy myself through possession?"
—Ertai, wizard adept

"They are 'between' in every way."
—Lyna, Soltari emissary

"You see our world when you shut your eyes so tightly that tiny shapes float before them."
—Lyna, to Ertai

"Ill luck and poor geography caught the Thalakos between us and the Dauthi."
—Lyna, Soltari emissary

"Gone today, here tomorrow."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"Let's do it again!"
—Squee, goblin cabin hand
It is said that the wind will blow the world past if you wait long enough.
Battles are won in nuance.

"In a world of untruths, the living lie rules."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"I followed her song only to find it was a dirge."
—Crovax

"Flying like a bird does not make you as free as one."
—Volrath

Orim regarded Gerrard coolly. "You are like the drake," she said, her expression unchanging. "It works hard to maintain its position, but to us it seems to glide along effortlessly. You *must* do the same."

"Everything around here has cut a deal with gravity."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
As Gerrard's form vanished into the maw of trees, Hanna mouthed a silent plea, mourning a crushed dream.
"You are wrong," Volrath said. "I do not hate the living. They often prove quite useful to me." And then he laughed.
"Once they've marked you," Starke said, "the world is made of glass."

"One would think I would be accustomed to unexpected returns."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator

"There's very little that escapes me, Greven. And you will escape very little if you fail."
—Volrath

"Rage is the only freedom left me."
—Greven *il*-Vec

"It is the way of most wizards to begin by exiling themselves and to end by exiling everyone else."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator

"If there is such a thing as too much power, I have not discovered it."
—Volrath

"In this dark place, yes, I *am* afraid of my own shadow."
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*

"The Dauthi army grows by screams and bounds."
—Lyna, Soltari emissary

"The Dauthi came from beneath the Ruins one night, and the darkness cast them in the best possible light."
—Soltari *Tales of Life*

"The Dauthi believe they dignify murder by paying for it."
—Lyna, Soltari emissary

"They have knives for every soul."
—Lyna, Soltari emissary
As the sludge below began to shift and take shapes, Gerrard turned from the railing to Orim. "I suppose," he said, "it's a little too late for prayer, isn't it?"
Greven *il*-Vec lifted Vhati off his feet. "The fall will give you time to think on your failure."

"These moonless, foreign skies keep me in thrall. Dark whispers echo in the night, and I cannot resist."
—Selenia, dark angel
Crovax gazed upon the dead, and for one dark moment he saw a banquet.

"I have made Crovax weep; now I will make him scream. The pain will not end, but will bind him to me."
—Volrath
Crovax had witnessed Selenia lead the *Predator* to the *Weatherlight*. As the battle raged on deck, he felt his strength melt in the heat of her betrayal.

"I once had an entire race killed just to listen to the rattling of their dried bones as I waded through them."
—Volrath

"Tell me again why you failed to capture Gerrard, you worthless pile of spine."
—Volrath, to Greven
A full coffin is like a full coffer—both are attractive to thieves.

Fall like night upon the foe.
—Motto of the Knights of Dusk
From the mists it rises, into the mists it retreats; through the mists it walks, fearless and unseen.

"They share more than their thoughts. We must shatter their link quickly!"
—Hanna, to Orim

"There will come a time when the voices of soil and seedling will sing only laments."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
The moans of the Death Pits were underscored by the chattering of imps, for whom the ship was cause for much discussion.

"These rains cannot quench; they carve the land's face like a scalpel on flesh."
—Crovax

"These creatures offer new challenges in the scrutiny of entrails."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"You will learn to earn death."
—Volrath

"My plan's elegance leads my enemies to believe it is spite that fuels me."
—Volrath

"First blood isn't as important as last blood."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

"They are called 'fowl' for a reason."
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*

"Volrath is a harsh master. My reflection is a constant reminder of that."
—Greven *il*-Vec

"If it tastes one drop of elvish blood I will cast it from the shroud to see it burn."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
Don't drink and thrive.

"This one has not screamed enough to show effective implantation. Kill it."
—Volrath

"Every act of destruction has a repercussion."
—Karn, silver golem
Ertai volunteered to open the portal. He figured he owed it one.

"There is a future in which I can see only mist and a single shadow."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
Spans of spines leapt from one sliver to the next, forming a deadly hedge around the *Weatherlight*.

"When Torahn bellows, none survive—not even the warrior whose horns he rides."
—Talruum adage

"The fishers will throw out their nets and draw them back filled with dust."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
"These runes are tough enough without the distraction," Ertai muttered, one eye on the drake.
"Relative of yours?" Ertai teased. Mirri simply sneered.
It is the forge of kings.

"Carrion! Keep your distance. My blade will come to you!"
—Crovax

"If they don't pinch, they burn. Can't ya eat any of da bugs here?"
—Squee, goblin cabin hand

"Remember the moral of the fireslinger fable: with power comes isolation."
—Karn, silver golem

When the first of these giants woke from the bedrock, he was still sleepy. He yawned and stretched until his legs grew so thin that they snapped like icicles in the sun.
—Vec lore
The Furnace of Rath is periodically illuminated by their sparkling yawns.

"Where I come from, stone stays on the ground."
—Tahngarth of the *Weatherlight*
"Crovax seems filled only with shadows," thought Orim. "Where does his strength come from?"
One mogg to aim the catapult, one mogg to steer the rock.
The match between Tahngarth and Greven was close only in the mind of the minotaur.
As Orim put the lightning rod into place on the bow, she cast a spell of protection to shield herself from the heat. That's when the Furnace got personal.
Gerrard looked all around for the source of the mysterious pulse, and at that moment the slivers boiled forth from the crevasses.
The first morning after acquiring her familiar, the wizard awoke with fleabites and mange.
Hope of deliverance is scorched by the fire of futility.

"Those who fear the darkness have never seen what the light can do."
—Selenia, dark angel
A lightning elemental once killed an entire tribe of merfolk—simply by going for a swim.
"Faugh!" snorted Tahngarth. "Why would it make a meal of something like you?" Squee looked relieved. "No," he continued, "you'd make a much better toothpick."

"Torahn's horns! They've seen us. Now, statue, you must fight to save yourself!"
—Tahngarth, aboard the *Predator*
"I got it! I got it! I—"
The evisceration of one mogg always cheers up the rest.
As they crept into the *Weatherlight*'s hold, the squad leader held up his hand and whispered, "Stop, goblins—what's that sound?"
As Gerrard and Greven neared each other, the moggs caught between them realized they should flee.
The third time the Oracle glanced suspiciously at him, Starke decided she had glanced twice too often.
The old Vec tell tales of a beast that fed on scraps but turned its nose up at the lavish banquet they set in its honor.
Wrap the flame as twine Kingdoms will be thine.

"His tongue must be honey, the way he gathers ants to fight with him."
—Volrath
"Such rage," thought Vhati, gazing up at the thunderhead from the *Predator*. "It is Greven's mind manifest."

"I used to describe something stable as 'rock solid.' So much for *that* expression."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

"Fire cleanses as well as destroys; that is the nature of change."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"You've not seen a storm until you've seen the kind that roars between worlds."
—Lyna, Soltari emissary

"Such fuss over machines, Gerrard. Remember that you are the prize of the Legacy. Throw away your toys!"
—Orim, Samite healer

"I know to whom I owe the most loyalty, and I see him in the mirror every day."
—Starke

"The land shall beg for drink and curse the rain that follows."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"I concede it was a cheap shot, but it was the only one I could afford."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
The *Predator* roared like an unruly beast, and the *Weatherlight* suddenly listed. "No!" screamed Hanna.

"Taste my horns!"
—Tahngarth of the *Weatherlight*

"You deify nature as female—kind and gentle—yet you cringe at what is natural."
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*

"The injury was being caught between this world and our own; the insult was to find walls within."
—Lyna, Soltari emissary

Wurm heads appear
Wild wurm near
Wurm tails you see
Wild wurm flee

Squee bounced up and down. "I sees a horsey, an' a piggy, an' a—"
"If you don't shut up," hissed Mirri, "you'll see a kidney and a spleeny."
Monkeys three, monkeys through.

"Like a sugar stick with wings!"
—Squee, goblin cabin hand

"I think I used up all my good luck and all my bad luck in the same fall."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

"We know our place in the cycle of life—and it is not as flies."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves

"Is it wrong to go straight for what you want? Sneaking is for cats and goblins."
—Tahngarth of the *Weatherlight*

"One day we shall walk where once was water."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
These are its last days. Mourning is over. Rage remains.
Few of Rath's rivers follow a steady course, so many new channels are carved for them.

"The land gives up little, but we are masters of persuasion."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
The mushroom wine made Gerrard's head spin, and his stomach soon followed suit.

"We have been patient. We have planned our attack. We are ready . . . *now*."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves

"If a creature is dumb enough to love you for leashing it, why would you want to follow its lead?"
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*
Too many choices will always distract a greedy beast.
"But *why* can't I get one?" sniveled Squee. "All da bugs here got wings."

"If the druids are so devoted to their trees, I will carve them coffins from their precious heartwood."
—Volrath
Changing Rath's landscape is like tearing the scab from a wound.
To snare what lies between worlds takes the patient reach of trees.
Wind in the trees is soothing, but the same can't be said for trees on the wind.

"In all my years in Llanowar I never understood where trees fit in. They are revered by elves and watered on by dogs."
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*
A bristling wave of slivers broke against the *Weatherlight*'s timbers.

"A perfect reflection of its world: brutal, fetal, and lacking truth."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
Hanna was astounded. Mirri read every leaf and wisp of breeze like a book of ancient lore.
The air was filled with the cracks and snaps of flesh hardening as the new sliver joined the battle.
Mirri listened intently, even as Hanna held the healing water to her lips. Would the sound of the spring drown out the elves' approach?

"One day the land will don the semblance of flesh and challenge even the plowshare's blade."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
The rain is driven like nails.

"You want to know your enemy? Look at your feet while you trample him."
—Tahngarth of the *Weatherlight*

"No fair! Since when does a bug get ta munch on *me*?"
—Squee, goblin cabin hand
Rath forces plants from its surface as one presses whey from cheese.

"See how *you* like it."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"Let Volrath choke on his crop of hatred."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
"If they board us we're finished," warned Orim. Crovax nodded. "And if they don't . . . what then?"

"We should step up repairs. I think the forest has plans for us."
—Crovax
As Gerrard made his escape, the wurm covered his flight by helping itself to three great mouthfuls of merfolk.
If you try to sneak up on a rootwalla, you'll suddenly find yourself dealing with twice the lizard.
It possesses no intelligence, only counter-intelligence.

"We shun them not for their dream but for their refusal to let such a noble dream die a noble death."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves

"It is our duty to endure."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves

"Just as you see the grave and remember the friend, I see this forest and remember Llanowar."
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*
The elves and merfolk have nothing but bitterness for each other. The trolls, however, find them both rather tasty.
The calmest day on Rath would be thought a storm anywhere else.
These are its last days. Better to grow broad and heavy. Better that the enemy is crushed beneath its carcass.

"Peace will come, but whether born of harmony or entropy I cannot say."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
These are its last days. But it will not go quietly.

Burl, scurf, and bower
Birth fern and flower.

"Only the most sophisticated inventions can survive nature's unsophisticated motivations."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator

Summer is buried there, centuries deep;
A crypt of years where seasons sleep.

"The path of least resistance will seldom lead you beyond your doorstep."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"If only we could so easily leave behind those parts of ourselves that pain us."
—Crovax

"I am light. I am dark. I must give my life to serve; not even death can release me."
—Selenia, dark angel

"Like a strain of music: easy to remember but impossible to catch."
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*
"Heat of battle" is usually a metaphor.
"Sir, I just thought . . . ," explained Vhati. "Don't think," interrupted Greven. "It doesn't suit you."

"It is not that you will go mad. It is that you will beg for madness."
—Volrath

"I am reminded of the fable of the silver egg. Its owner cracks it open to see what jewels it holds, only to discover a simple yellow yolk."
—Karn, silver golem
The bite of the tinviper feels most like a razor drawn across the tongue.
It is like life and destiny: we think we know the story, but we have read only half the tale.
Like a kettle set to boil, it must eventually go off—on someone.
The sculptor, weary of his work, created art that would finish itself.
Squee: "What's that?" Ertai: "It's a magical book." Squee: "Am I smart enough ta use it?" Ertai: "You could say that."

"Memory is a burden that wears at the soul as weather wears at stone."
—Crovax
"Here."
"Hard to imagine," mused Hanna, stroking the petal, "such a lovely flower inspiring such greed."
Hanna regarded Squee sternly. "Because it's *not* a toy, no matter how much it may look like one," she said, taking the manakin from him.
When the clever counterfeit was accepted by the hive, Volrath's influence upon the slivers grew even stronger.
Moggs never volunteer for anything twice.

"Just when I get them working, they always start fighting and tearing at each other for spare parts."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator
Every page cost a life; every secret cost a thousand more.

"They are convenient in having no souls, but less so in having no spirit."
—Volrath
"Have no illusions," Volrath warned Greven, "about free will."

"This has nothing to do with what you know and everything to do with what I wish."
—Volrath
As the horrors closed in on Gerrard, Squee trembled and clutched his toy for comfort. He didn't know where it came from or why it was so warm, but he was glad he'd kept it near.

Time passes, time crawls;
Time doesn't move at all.
After losing several of the devices to midair collisions, Greven forbade moggs from operating telethopters.

"We will start small, I think."
—Volrath
Its growl is a long, rumbling grind of gears and clockwork, its bark a blast of hissing steam.

There is no glory to be gained in the kingdom of the dead.
—Vec tomb inscription

"The air here smells like a grave."
—Crovax

"The reflection of land interests me far more than its reality."
—Volrath

"The land promises nothing and keeps its promise."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"I just hope this isn't another wild turtle chase!"
—Vernon Fenwick
"Utroms . . . Triceratons . . . there's little difference to me. I help one destroy the other, pick up the pieces, then get them the hell off of my planet."

"Never been defeated, huh? Well, you never tangled with a turtle before!"
—Donatello
Azrael was born on the wind to guide others to new beginnings.
"HI! I'm Pete!"
"Of course I know what you did! You always do precisely what I told you not to do!"
"Everything you know, I have shown you, but I have not shown you everything I know."

"Nice to meet you, Botticelli . . . or whatever your name is. Tell your boss to send some scarier goons next time."
—Ace Duck
"Splinter said that, once, ninjas defended the poor and the weak from power. We could be real ninjas. We can fight for the people!"
"Hello, prey."
They stood beside him. Whether they were figments or true spirits no longer mattered.
"That's right. Eyes on me."
For a moment, there is only relentless snow and frozen breath.

"Yer right. We're just a scrappy band of mutants. We can't win. But boy, can we stir up trouble."
—Old Hob

"As far as I'm concerned, Pepperoni's one of us!"
—Raphael
"I wanna make things better for everyone. No more squalor. No more fear."
"For the glory of the Republic!"

"See you around the multiverse, bros."
—One Leonardo or another
Other perspectives can help one find the proper direction.
In the fight between mutants, ninjas, and aliens, don't underestimate a resourceful human.
"Freelance reporting pays even worse than tutoring, but the satisfaction of uncovering the truth makes it all worth it! Also the free ringside tickets to cover intergalactic wrestling don't suck."
Designed for autonomous pollination, the Stocktronics buzz bot's souped-up power plant allows for months of independent service. The optional taser is for defensive purposes only, of course.

"Wondering what I've got in the box? Pain, soldier! And lots of it!"
—Herman

"My son, for someone so intelligent, the obvious often eludes you."
—Splinter
"Unfortunately, the lowly turtle has been saddled by society with the stereotype of being velocity challenged."
"I'll need my bag of tricks."
A freak accident transferred Professor Honeycutt's mind into his robot assistant. Blamed for his own death, he fled . . . as the FUGITOID!
"You hunger for retribution, I know. And so I come to you with an offering . . ."
"Like a monster seeking prey in the night, the truth will hunt you down."
Metalhead simulates dozens of fighting styles, including Foot ninjutsu.

"You will experience some discomfort. Then, for better or worse, the concepts of comfort and discomfort will become quite alien."
—Fugitoid
"Stealth-o-rama, huh? Righteous."
"You guys seriously try to do this with jump kicks?"
Lab safety is everyone's business.
"You guys don't get sick during time travel, do you?"

"We strike hard and fade away into the night."
—Leonardo
No one in New York was going to notice one more cockroach.

"When are we now?"
—Donatello
Using exoskeletons and false skins, the utroms took up residence on Earth after their ship crashed. Returning home using only Earth's primitive technology has proven challenging.

"Question: Do you like penicillin on your pizza?"
—Donatello
"I am ancient efficiency. I am evolution's future. I am mutation come full, vicious circle!"

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Exile target creature card from your graveyard. Create a token that's a copy of it, except it isn't legendary and is a Mutant in addition to its other types.
II, III — Create a token that's a copy of a card exiled with this Saga, except it isn't legendary and is a Mutant in addition to its other types.

faces.f: Often enemies, always brothers . . . till the end.
"We've drained human life force for millennia. Then one day, turtles! Delectable! We'll suck you dry and spit out the shells!"
Mashima would protect the soul of Oroku Saki at any cost.
"We suffered a bit of a setback tonight, but rest assured: We'll have the planet purged and primed for you right on schedule."
Your instructor is Casey Jones!
"When I am done, there will be no evidence that you ever existed!"
The Kuro Kabuto has been the symbol of Foot Clan leadership since its inception over 1,500 years ago.
"Tonight I dine on turtle soup."
Snake-Eyes's gift takes others back to their worst memory. To the weak, it is a curse; to the wise, a second chance.
"Possess the right thinking. Only then can one receive the gifts of strength, knowledge, and peace."
It's best to never discover what they squirrel away.

"These guys are good!"
—Leonardo
"I have molded myself into perfection, Hamato. Look upon me, and know fear."
The Rat King's subjects are everywhere you don't want to be.

"Well, I'd say we redecorated the place nicely!"
—Raphael
The power of the Foot is its ability to infiltrate every system from the shadows.
"Goongala!"
"Lord Krang, we arrive. We obey. We conquer."
It was fitting that the most dangerous turtle bore a weapon of peace.

"I want rock 'n' roll, man! Lucky I brought my own drumsticks . . ."
—Casey Jones
"Being a mutant isn't easy. Lucky for me, I've been preparing for this my entire life!"
"SAY YER PRAYERS, TOITLES!"

"For me, all things remain strictly business. And today's business happens to be extermination!"
—Baxter Stockman

"Hmmm . . . How many should I send? Three? Five? Ten, maybe!"
—Baxter Stockman
After the Bomb's take on thrash metal isn't for everyone . . . and Sheena wouldn't have it any other way.

"I'm a company woman. I'm part of the plan. I'm part of the team. And I enjoy my work."
—Zodi
"This is us against them, plain and simple. Either you're with us, or . . ."

"These guys are young, but no rookies. They've fought and beat everything on two legs in this area . . . except us."
—Leonardo
"You guys must be studying the abridged book of ninja fighting."
"Time to punch in."

"Anger is a dangerous ally. It clouds your judgment. You need to control it, lest it control you."
—Splinter
"Change of plans!"

"The mousers have a new command: to consume everything here . . . all of you will be destroyed!"
—Baxter Stockman
Catching enemies between a rock and a hard place.
"Tell 'em you've got a new partner. One who knows the true meaning of being a warrior."

"Yeah, I threw in some habaneros to cut the heat on this."
—Raphael
"Tell me, Screwloose, aren't we good? Mmhm. So, wouldn't that make them evil? Right!"
Forgiveness is divine, but never pay full price for late pizza.
When you're open to new things, a weird world of wonder unfolds before you.

"With faithful Alberto's assistance, this shall be a gathering of untold delight! Why would you ever wish to leave?"
—Toad Baron
"Whatever my lil' man D.B. here can't dig under, I can just about bust through. Ain't no one caging us ever again."

"There is no fear in my heart. I will overcome even this challenge!"
—Leonardo

"A teacher must be ready to accept responsibility for the student, especially when the student is a weirdo."
—Splinter
"I felt kind of excited about being mutated, you know? I was getting to have this once in a lifetime experience! Maybe I could even base my thesis on it . . ."
"We live together, we train together, we fight together, we stand together . . . We are ninjas."
"Uno, Moja, Odyn, and Yi carry on the brothers' legacy. New York will be free once more."

"Have at me, and we will find out who is the fittest among us."
—Manmoth
Bebop and Rocksteady's new Cretaceous stowaway quickly developed a taste for leftovers . . . and ears.

"I LOVE being a turtle!"
—Michelangelo
"Get back, all ya'll! Stay away from me! I ain't safe, ya hear! Ain't no friend! I'm a monster!"
The nature of a giant, disembodied cyborg cow head that travels through time and space raises countless questions. But Cudley doesn't like talking with his mouth full.
Unnoticed by the crowd, the strange canister bounced several more times, striking and smashing a glass jar which held four small turtles . . .
Built from scraps. Defined by self.
They imagine that out beyond the zoo, beyond the pen, there exists another world, and it encroaches with rapid certainty upon their own . . .
"You flatter me, Ms. O'Neil. I like that."
"They'll beat you with fists, with a bat, with a knife. / So don't try to stop them, just run for your life! / Get set and get ready, / For Bebop and Rocksteady!"
Technician. Tactician.
"Rest your brains, Donnie, I got my own idea."
Not all humans fear the unknown. The Earth Protection Force specializes in teaching the unknown to fear them instead.
The Foot Elite are the personal students of the Shredder, a reserve guard without equal.
"Free our brothers! The human reign of terror around here ends tonight!"

"That's not what they mean by 'pet food,' dude!"
—Michelangelo

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Destroy all creatures.
II — Mill four cards. When you do, return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand.
III — Whenever a creature you control attacks alone this turn, put three +1/+1 counters on it. It gains trample, lifelink, and indestructible until end of turn.

faces.f:
"Everyone's got their own strengths, Lita. You never know what cards they might play. Instead, focus on what you know and never doubt your choices."
—Michelangelo

"This is absolutely ridiculous, Saki! They aren't meant for riding! What happened to the ninja's famous subtlety?"
—Baxter Stockman
Their strength hailed not from what they shared, but from how their differences complemented one another.
Designed to get rodents out of small spaces, its Mouser maws can be used to seize all sorts of vermin!
"I don't need a name. I'm nobody."
Glyph has claimed to be a survivor of an alien war, a deposed minister of weather, and the last of the dinosaurs. Whatever the truth, his origin stories always bear a lesson.
"Weirdo ninjas got some nerve showing up on our turf. Sayin' they don't wanna fight but they got swords and stuff. Heh."

"Beats working in the sewers. Too many freaky mutants down there."
—Muckman
At odds as brothers, perfectly in sync as fighters.

"The Slithery! He's snatches little kids an' keeps 'em in cages! He don't got no legs and just slithers."
—Lita
"The first rule of the ninja is 'do no harm.' Unless you need to do harm. Then do lots of harm!"

"Spray them with the anti-mutagen? No, no. I'm afraid ingestion is the only course."
—Dr. Jordan Perry
"Master say have fun . . ."
"Broadcast: Seized. Initiate seek-and-destroy protocols."
"Apologies for the disturbance, [INCIDENTAL WITNESS], have a pleasant day!"
The Molecular Amplification technology of Krang's exo-suit allows him to expand and adapt not only his tactics, but his physical form.

"And just a sprig of parsley for color . . ."
—Michelangelo
"Why skate a half-pipe when you can skate a sewer pipe?"
Even unfinished, the Technodrome was magnificent, a wonder of alien technology.

"Hey, in crazy backwards land, crazy backwards dude is king."
—Michelangelo

"I hear the sewers in Connecticut are really nice."
—Michelangelo

"Getting inside will be easy. Getting to Shredder might even be doable. Getting back out? That's going to be hard."
—April O'Neil
Their recipe isn't the only secret.

"Until we completely understand the mutagenic agent's effects, these people must remain contained for our health and safety."
—Baxter Stockman
The light from the Translocation Matrix could be seen throughout the city. The utroms knew they only had a brief window to escape after its accidental activation.
Home is where your pizza delivers.
"See you on the other side, bros."
"We Turtles don't know the meaning of the word defeat."
"I got no problem with you, but I think my friends here just might . . ."
"I can figure this out! Don't worry about me—ow!"
"I've been working on a pan-dimensional portal of my own. It's the real thing. Of course, I haven't actually tested it yet . . ."
"Who needs Foot soldiers? I can subdue you with your own fancy footwork."
"You don't have to explain it to me, I'm the one who invented it!"
"So sorry to bring our game to an early conclusion. You wouldn't have won anyway."
"Behold the secret technique only taught to true masters of the Foot Clan."
"Maybe they've forgotten what a great scientist I used to be, but I don't forget."
"I'll teach you criminals to befoul our sewers!"
"Of course it's dangerous. That's the whole point of a weapon!"
"Alright, time out! Who's fighting who again?"

"Mosey along, critters. You're blockin' my way!"
—Groundchuck
"Drop in anytime, micro-dudes."
April's Turtle tots: Moja, Odyn, Uno, and Yi.
"We got a score to settle with you little twerps."
"Hey, watch it, Leonardo. You're ruining my finish!"
A good ninja can defend themselves with anything.

"The ninja who loses his temper, loses the battle."
—Karai
"Face it, Leo, this is the only job we're qualified for."
The Path of the Four Winds is a quest for knowledge. South to the serpent. West to the Jaguar. North to the dragon. East to the eagle.

"You losers better talk, or else I'm gonna get sarcastic!"
—Raphael
"You have corrupted my teachings. Now you will pay for your crimes."
"Master say have fun!"
"Utroms . . . Triceratons . . . there's little difference to me. I help one destroy the other, pick up the pieces, then get them the hell off of my planet."

"As far as I'm concerned, Pepperoni's one of us!"
—Raphael

"See you around the multiverse, bros."
—One Leonardo or another
"You hunger for retribution, I know. And so I come to you with an offering . . ."

"When are we now?"
—Donatello
"I am ancient efficiency. I am evolution's future. I am mutation come full, vicious circle!"
"We suffered a bit of a setback tonight, but rest assured: We'll have the planet purged and primed for you right on schedule."
"When I am done, there will be no evidence that you ever existed!"
Snake-Eyes's gift takes others back to their worst memory. To the weak, it is a curse; to the wise, a second chance.

"I want rock 'n' roll, man! Lucky I brought my own drumsticks . . ."
—Casey Jones

"The mousers have a new command: to consume everything here . . . all of you will be destroyed!"
—Baxter Stockman
The nature of a giant, disembodied cyborg cow head that travels through time and space raises countless questions. But Cudley doesn't like talking with his mouth full.
Unnoticed by the crowd, the strange canister bounced several more times, striking and smashing a glass jar which held four small turtles . . .
"Broadcast: Seized. Initiate seek-and-destroy protocols."

YOU DID IT!
Get out the toploaders,
you opened a God Pack.
Nauctis: The Sunken Realm
Bitter vengeance never glowed so bright nor sang so sweet.
The very skies seethe with the aven's hatred for the Cabal.
By definition, madness ends in one of two ways: clarity . . . or death.
"I am the holy wind that shall avenge the Cabal's victims."

"The spirits of the righteous shall rise into the sky. Even dirtwalkers will fly like aven."
—Major Teroh
They soar, and the mystics follow.

"Inhale life. Exhale pain."
—Mystic elder
"How to punish the guilty is up to the Ancestor. Deciding who merits such punishment is up to me."
Don't mistake isolation for safety.
The light of reason follows them even into battle.
Teroh dreams of his enemies' doom.

"He smiles with poisoned lips."
—Empress Llawan
Some tides need no moon.

"Power, gold, crackers—every bird has its price."
—Chainer, dementia master
The ideas came flooding in so fast that they couldn't all be contained.
It's easy to tell the difference between the devious cephalids and the trustworthy ones. The trustworthy ones are dead.
The cautious are wary of their enemies. The wise are also wary of their friends.

"Magic is like the tide—both ebb, both flow, and both serve my whims."
—Empress Llawan
"The specimen seems to be broken."

"My enemies will forget everything but their anguish."
—Ambassador Laquatus
In front of every strong leader is a pool of loyal bodyguards.

"The only kind of water that should fly through the air is rain."
—Kamahl, pit fighter
The question strained his sanity. The answer snapped it in half.
"Are you thinking what I'm thinking?"
An army from a soldier, a flock from a bird, a school from a fish . . . a profit from an atrocity.
"I am as the wind that bears me: harsh yet gentle, fleeting yet ever-present. Together we fly beyond imagination."
Just because your eyes are open doesn't mean you're awake.
Laquatus dreams of seizing control.

"Each syllable chills your veins. Each word rattles your mind."
—Cabal Patriarch
"Clerics give up when their patients die. Can I help it if I'm more compassionate?"

"Just what I need—more competition."
—Cabal grave robber
Since it eats only carrion, sometimes it needs to make some from scratch.
The pits have their own form of mercy.
Chainer dreams of ultimate knowledge.
Chainer's dark gift to a darker soul.
When you get into the swamp, the swamp gets into you.
The crowd roared, the fighters bled, and the dead piled high in the pits. Only the Cabal could win.

"They appreciate my handiwork. I hear their joy in every scream."
—Chainer, dementia master

"If the Nantuko only knew what awaits them beyond death, they would abandon all they hold dear."
—Cabal Patriarch
It knows what makes you tick. It knows how to make the ticking stop.
Braids dreams of dark rebirth.
Empires rise and fall, but evil is eternal.
Chainer's madness personified, it exists only to slaughter the innocent.
The Patriarch dreams of vile plague.
Don't confuse lunacy with courage.

"Don't let your mind wander—it might not come back."
—Braids, dementia summoner
Chainer's insanity touched nearly every living thing—including viruses.
Some zombies are natural-reborn leaders.

"I've seen lightning move slower."
—Nomad sentry

"I like to think of him as concentrated barbarian."
—Kamahl, pit fighter

"We offer power to anyone willing to take it. Sadly, few are unburdened enough by their prejudices to accept."
—Cabal surgeon
It adds injury to injury.

"The longer it's caged, the madder it gets."
—Firecat handler
Kamahl dreams of storms of fire.
Captive dwarves always regain their freedom, either through escape or through a desperate, fiery death.
"Fools dig for water, corpses, or gold. The earth's real treasure is far deeper."
He doesn't slow until his spear is weighted with corpses.
Its blast can fuse armor to bone, leaving skeletons that glint brightly in the sun.

"Trickery can't defeat raw power."
—Matoc, lavamancer
Otaria's epidemic of insanity didn't affect certain barbarians—but no one noticed.
"We've been taught that strength is everything. So how can an alliance with the strongest be a betrayal?"
He gets to the point right away.
Its material may not be precious, but the minds it protects are.

"A good whack on the head usually has the same effect."
—Kamahl, pit fighter
Krosa's topmost bottom feeder.
It's hard to be humble when the whole world is bite size.
He wears his scars like badges of honor, warning his foes that he's not easily defeated.

None can find what hasn't been lost.
—Nantuko teaching

"Finesse is no match for brute force."
—Seton, centaur druid
Krosan druids do not fear death, for they know that nature will only prosper from their passing.

"It's a slithering, coldblooded menace. I've gotta respect that."
—Braids, dementia summoner
Seton dreams of life renewed.
Deep within the Cabal's vault, the Mirari pulsed like a dead sun—and its darkness radiated across Otaria.

n: Bounty: Gorra Tash and Silas // Wanted!

faces.f: Only the warrior who can admit mortal weakness will be bolstered by immortal strength.

"My family sheltered in her light, the dark was content to wait."
—Crovax

Hanna: "We must learn how they protect each other."
Mirri: "After they're done trying to kill us, all right?"

"I always charge a little extra to take on a pegasus. They fly like eagles, kick like mules, and hide like hermits."
—Tahli *en*-Dal, bounty hunter
Takara shook with guilt. She knew the last image her father had seen was her sword flashing toward him.
The *Weatherlight* dragged the Predator behind it, the cradle hauling the casket.
"Hope shall be the blade that severs our bonds."
It was not the minotaur's shoulders but his soul that bore the heaviest weight.
The swarm seemed unmoved by the artificial slivers' destruction. "They clearly were not the leaders," Hanna cursed. "I guess we'll have to do this the hard way."
If dragons excel at anything more than vanity, it is greed.
"Forgive me," Mirri whispered. "I thought you a burden, and you saved my life." Hanna quietly accepted the apology.
Gerrard grinned and drew his sword. "This won't be a fair fight," he called to his crew. "They should have brought a second ship!"

"One cannot cleanse the wounds of failure."
—Karn, silver golem
The true treasure no thief can touch.

"A skilled decoy can throw your enemies off your trail. A master decoy can survive to do it again."
—Gerrard of the Weatherlight
The kor forsake roots for the winding of the path, forsake voices for the silence of the mind, forsake all else for the poverty of isolation.

"The silkworm spins itself a new existence. So the healer weaves the threads of life."
—Orim, Samite healer
Frozen by conscience, Karn did not resist as the moggs carried him to the Predator.
"Our belief shall be the lance that pierces Volrath's heart."
"The cannon wasn't aimed at you!" pleaded Vhati. "I'm not sure which is more pathetic," replied Greven, "your judgment or your aim."
Shackles of gold are still shackles.

"You've got your childhood wish at last. Now you get to die."
—Gerrard, to Volrath

"In times of war the victors rarely save their best for last."
—Gerrard of the Weatherlight

"Prayer rarely explains."
—Orim, Samite healer
"In Rath," the priest said, "there is even greater need for prayer."

"Dauthi blood is soltari wine."
—Soltari Tales of Life

Death free throat from thirst, mouth from speech, feet from earth.
—Kor requiem
The less you have, the harder you fight for it.

"Hold your position! Leave doubt for the dying!"
—Tahngarth of the Weatherlight

The ceiling and the floor fell in love, but only the wall knew.
—Dal saying
Only a matter as vital as destroying Volrath could bring together the reclusive kor people.

"There shall be a vast shout and then a vaster silence."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"Let no child be without a sword. We will all fight, for if we fail, we will certainly all die."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"It was probably a lousy spell in the first place."
—Ertai, wizard adept
All Mirri wanted to do was rest, but she couldn't ignore a nagging suspicion as she followed Crovax's skulking form.

"There is nothing you can do that I cannot simply deny."
—Ertai, wizard adept
Within without.

"To think that some find sleep a restful state."
—Volrath
From nothing came teeth.
Two things are needed to survive the harsh skies of Rath: a thick hide and a thicker skull.

"It's hard to hurt anyone when you're as transparent as your motives."
—Ertai, wizard adept
Cross the eyes of a hammerhead and you'll dot its teeth.

"So like men are they: a hardened shell with fragile flesh beneath."
—Selenia, dark angel
Hunger is like the sea: deep, endless, and unforgiving.
Squee tucked the warm ball in his pocket and slipped a pebble in its place. "Glok," he mumbled, and hid.

"The fatal flaw in every plan is the assumption that you know more than your enemy."
—Volrath
From its maw comes neither word nor whisper—only wind.

"Part of me believes that Barrin taught me meditation simply to shut me up."
—Ertai, wizard adept
In the depths of Rootwater, salvage and sewage differ only in texture.

"A jigsaw puzzle that lives, breeds, and thinks."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator

"Bitter water, vicious wave;
Shadow-cold shallows, root-made maze.
Home's angry embrace."
—Rootwater Saga

"History is a potent weapon."
—Karn, silver golem
Water is life. Or perhaps it is just something to wash it down with.

"Twice I have let the Legacy slip away. Never again."
—Karn, silver golem
Call it the thinking mage's version of brute force.
They drift in and out of shadow and ever on toward madness.

"You see our world when you shut your eyes so tightly that tiny shapes float before them."
—Lyna, to Ertai

"Gone today, here tomorrow."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"Let's do it again!"
—Squee, goblin cabin hand
It is said that the wind will blow the world past if you wait long enough.
Battles are won in nuance.

"No home, no heart, no hope."
—Stronghold graffito

"I followed her song only to find it was a dirge."
—Crovax

"Flying like a bird does not make you as free as one."
—Volrath

Orim regarded Gerrard coolly. "You are like the drake," she said, her expression unchanging. "It works hard to maintain its position, but to us it seems to glide along effortlessly. You must do the same."

"Everything around here has cut a deal with gravity."
—Gerrard of the Weatherlight
"Mine."
Eating is all it knows.

"One would think I would be accustomed to unexpected returns."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator

"There's very little that escapes me, Greven. And you will escape very little if you fail."
—Volrath
"Rage is the only freedom left to me."
A farewell to arms . . . and feet . . . and legs . . .

"It is the way of most wizards to begin by exiling themselves and to end by exiling everyone else."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator

"If there is such a thing as too much power, I have not discovered it."
—Volrath

"All dauthi are jackals, regardless of breed."
—Lyna, soltari emissary

"The dauthi came from beneath the ruins one night, and the darkness cast them in the best possible light."
—Soltari Tales of Life

"They have knives for every soul."
—Lyna, soltari emissary
As the sludge below began to shift and take shapes, Gerrard turned from the railing to Orim. "I suppose," he said, "it's a little too late for prayer, isn't it?"
For a sharp second, Selenia froze, and Crovax's blade found home. As the angel shattered like glass, Crovax felt his mind collapse—the curse had been fulfilled.
Life has always been a dance. It is only fitting that death sing the tune.
Greven *il*-Vec lifted Vhati off his feet. "The fall will give you time to think on your failure."
A sickness stirs in its eyes, a nightmare born in darkened wails.
"My ship . . . ," Sisay mumbled. "Intact," Gerrard reassured her, "which is more than I can say for you, my friend." Sisay laughed despite the pain.
A full coffin is like a full coffer—both are attractive to thieves.

"My enemies' death yields threefold benefit: removal, reuse, and research."
—Volrath

"These creatures offer new challenges in the scrutiny of entrails."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"You will learn to earn death."
—Volrath

"I am confined by sleep and defined by nightmare."
—Crovax

"Not again."
—Hans

"They are called 'fowl' for a reason."
—Mirri of the Weatherlight
A hiss before dying.

"If it tastes one drop of elvish blood I will cast it from the shroud to see it burn."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
The assassin sees only throats and hears only heartbeats.
"Just take a little off the top."
The hounds' barks are a horrifying chorus of screams, moans, and whispers.

"It is the nature of evil to turn you against yourself."
—Starke

"Every act of destruction has a repercussion."
—Karn, silver golem
"I'll take that. You won't need it when the revolution comes."
Spans of spines leapt from one sliver to the next, forming a deadly hedge around the Weatherlight.
"Relative of yours?" Ertai teased. Mirri simply sneered.

What is high as a mountain and low as a snake?
—Dal riddle

"Carrion! Keep your distance. My blade will come to you!"
—Crovax

"I hear the roaring of a wave whose waters are red and whose mists are black."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"Remember the fable of the elf who came upon a cave of gold. In trying to free the largest piece, she was crushed by its weight."
—Karn, silver golem
Once these horrifying creatures were perfected, there was no need for armodons.

"Where I come from, stone stays on the ground."
—Tahngarth of the Weatherlight
Furnace air crackles with magmatic cackles.
One mogg to aim the catapult, one mogg to steer the rock.
Hope of deliverance is scorched by the fire of futility.

"Those who fear the darkness have never seen what the light can do."
—Selenia, dark angel
"Faugh!" snorted Tahngarth. "Why would it make a meal of something like you?" Squee looked relieved. "No," he continued, "you'd make a much better toothpick."
Living below a flowstone foundry produces a disproportionate number of fire mages among the il.
Only by sacrificing any semblance of defense could Gerrard best Greven.

"Torahn's horns! They've seen us. Now, statue, you must fight to save yourself!"
—Tahngarth, aboard the Predator
"I got it! I got it! I—"
They'll attack whatever's in front of them—as long as you tell them where that is.
Stand clear if he gets an itch.
Ogre shamans must be bright enough to learn their invocations and dim enough to use them.

"If we cannot live proudly, we die so!"
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
Wrap the flame as twine, Kingdoms will be thine.

"His tongue must be honey, the way he gathers ants to fight with him."
—Volrath
"Such rage," thought Vhati, gazing up at the thunderhead from the Predator. "It is Greven's mind manifest."
Most creatures grow out of their baby teeth, but sabertooth wyverns grow into theirs.

"I used to describe something stable as 'rock solid.' So much for that expression."
—Gerrard of the Weatherlight

"You've not seen a storm until you've seen the kind that roars between worlds."
—Lyna, soltari emissary

"Such fuss over machines, Gerrard. Remember that you are the prize of the Legacy. Throw away your toys!"
—Orim, Samite healer
A snap of fingers, a snap of teeth.

"I know to whom I owe the most loyalty, and I see him in the mirror every day."
—Starke

"I concede it was a cheap shot, but it was the only one I could afford."
—Gerrard of the Weatherlight

"The injury was being caught between this world and our own; the insult was to find walls within."
—Lyna, soltari emissary

Squee bounced up and down. "I sees a horsey, an' a piggy, an' a—"
"If you don't shut up," hissed Mirri, "you'll see a kidney and a spleeny."

"We know our place in the cycle of life—and it is not as flies."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
The hunter would never forget the time or place where he first met the carnassid, for they buried him there.
Bores ruin a party. Boars are party to ruin.
As the bough stretches, so shall you grow. As the roots spread, so shall you thrive.
These are its last days. It is doomed to be remembered only until the hunters hunger again.
Changing Rath's landscape is like tearing the scab from a wound.
To snare what lies between worlds takes the patient reach of trees.
Wind in the trees is soothing, but the same can't be said for trees on the wind.
Seeking the company of plants ensures that your wits will go to seed.
A bristling wave of slivers broke against the Weatherlight's timbers.

"A perfect reflection of its world: brutal, fetal, and lacking truth."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
Unlike their cousins, Rathi basilisks turn their victims into puddles of flowstone.

"Full of beauty and grace, with a predator's instincts . . . Although she wanders, I have always thought Mirri belongs in Llanowar most of all."
—Rofellos, Llanowar emissary
Hope is the one crop that can grow in any climate.
The air was filled with the cracks and snaps of flesh hardening as the new sliver joined the battle.
The rain is driven like nails.

"You want to know your enemy? Look at your feet while you trample him."
—Tahngarth of the Weatherlight
Mirri did not have time to think, only to react.
Rath forces plants from its surface as one presses whey from cheese.

"See how you like it."
—Ertai, wizard adept
As Gerrard made his escape, the wurm covered his flight by helping itself to three great mouthfuls of merfolk.
If you try to sneak up on a rootwalla, you'll suddenly find yourself dealing with twice the lizard.

"It is our duty to endure."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
The elves and merfolk have nothing but bitterness for each other. The trolls, however, find them both rather tasty.

"As it moved, the wurm's spines gathered up bits of flowstone, which took the shapes of dead villagers' heads. Each head spoke a single sound, but if taken together, they said, 'Alas for the living.'"
—Dal myth of the wurm
These are its last days. Better to grow broad and heavy. Better that the enemy is crushed beneath its carcass.

"Peace will come, but whether born of harmony or entropy I cannot say."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

Burl, scurf, and bower
Birth fern and flower.

"Only the most sophisticated inventions can survive nature's unsophisticated motivations."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator
Each flower identical, every leaf and petal disturbingly exact.
The first sliver burst against the cave wall, and others piled in behind to deepen the new tunnel.
Bred as living shields, these slivers have proven unruly—they know they cannot be caught.
Mogglings have been known to play ball with hibernating slivers, completely unaware of their true nature.
"I am light. I am dark. I must give my life to serve; not even death can release me."
Her children are ever part of her.

"Slivers are evil and slivers are sly; And if you get eaten, then no one will cry."
—Mogg children's rhyme
"Sir, I just thought . . . ," explained Vhati. "Don't think," interrupted Greven. "It doesn't suit you."
"We are kinfolk," explained Karn to the sliver queen. "Just as you need your progeny to complete you, so do I need the pieces of the Legacy to make me whole."

"I am reminded of the fable of the silver egg. Its owner cracks it open to see what jewels it holds, only to discover a simple yellow yolk."
—Karn, silver golem

"Hup, two, three, four,
Dunno how to count no more."
—Mogg march
The bite of the tinviper feels most like a razor drawn across the tongue.
